triggeringTask: Compress Phase 1 of plans/docs-quality-metrics-gap.plans.md
gap: When constructing multi-line file content via python -c @"..."@ or inline Node.js, PowerShell double-quoted here-strings interpret backtick-n (`n) as newline escapes. This caused backtick-quoted commands like `npm` to be mangled (e.g., `npm` became newline + pm) and corrupted generated Markdown files.
resolution: Switch to writing a temporary .mjs script file with the literal content and executing it with node, avoiding PowerShell here-string escaping entirely.
confirmation: Resolution verified by byte-level inspection; final files contain correct triple backticks and inline backtick quoting.
resumeAction: For Markdown writes with backticks, prefer file-based script execution over inline here-strings.

description: Integer TS constant interpolated into a GLSL const float initializer fails GLSL ES compile (const int -> const highp float). jsdom jest lanes mock WebGL so the compile failure was invisible to every green lane; only real-browser runShaderWarmup catches it. gap:
Two orchestration-level gaps were found while amending the Step 14J packet at contract level. (1) The consolidated `slice-advancement` gate runs exactly four TRIVIAL sub-gates (plan-sync, step-packet, plan-slice-quality, plan-command-lint) plus three FULL gates (shared-validation, code-coverage, specialist-review) - it does NOT include `convergence-tracker`. Yet `convergence-tracker` is the gate that reads the `fix-loop: <slice-id> iteration <n> status=<failed|passed>` markers under `## Latest validation evidence`, so a fix-loop cycle can be fully patched and re-gated with `slice-advancement` reporting 4/4 PASS while the tracker has never observed the cycle at all. The fix-loop markers must therefore be appended MANUALLY and `convergence-tracker` must be invoked separately. (2) The `step-packet` gate captures the `## Latest validation evidence` section with the regex /^## Latest validation evidence\s*?
([\s\S]*?)(?=?
## |$)/m - the `m` flag makes the lazy `(?=?
## |$)` alternative match the FIRST line boundary, so the capture is truncated to 1,160 characters (the first line only, ending at plan line 2917) and any green-light marker further down the section is invisible to that gate. `plan-readiness.gate.mjs` uses the same section pattern WITHOUT the `m` flag and correctly sees the whole 141 KB section, so the two gates disagree about the same plan state. The practical consequence: the authoring instance cannot self-record a verdict either way, which is consistent with the author/verify loop-ownership rule, but the truncation is a gate-side defect that should not be relied upon as a safety net.
resolution: Appended the fix-loop markers for the amended slices by hand at the `<!-- EVIDENCE-APPEND-POINT -->` marker inside `## Latest validation evidence`, outside any code fence and at the start of a line in the exact format `fix-loop: <slice-id> iteration <n> status=<failed|passed>`. Verified independently that `convergence-tracker` now counts them (`P1-crowd-red-contracts` iterationCount=1, `P1-crowd-row-level-host` iterationCount=2, both PASS). Recorded the `step-packet` m-flag truncation as a known gate-side defect in the plan evidence rather than attempting a gate change, since the standing planning-only mandate forbids editing gate scripts.
confirmation: Learning event appended; convergence-tracker re-run confirms the fix-loop markers are counted; slice-advancement re-run for all five Step 14J slices passes 4/4 TRIVIAL sub-gates each.
resumeAction: A future orchestration pass should either add `convergence-tracker` to the `slice-advancement` composite (or to a documented TRIVIAL/FULL set that includes it), and should fix the `step-packet` green-light capture regex by removing the `m` flag (or by anchoring the terminator with a non-multiline lookahead) so both gates read the same evidence section. Until then, plan authors must append fix-loop markers manually and must not treat the `step-packet` green-light warning as an authoritative readiness signal.

description: Git rule normalized across the agent surface to permit read-only inspection (status/diff/log/show/blame/rev-parse/ls-files; --no-pager permitted) while keeping every mutating command banned (add/commit/push/pull/fetch/checkout/reset/restore/revert/stash/clean/merge/rebase/apply). The prior blanket 'git is uninstalled' phrasing made safe read-only inspection look like a violation and pushed agents toward accidental worktree-reverting mutations.
evidence: 41 files amended: the normalized rule block ('## CRITICAL RULE - GIT: READ-ONLY INSPECTION ALLOWED, MUTATION BANNED') is now present in 41 files under .github - 39 .github/agents/*.agent.md files plus .github/ORCHESTRATION_GUIDE.md and .github/copilot-instructions.md - and the full banned-command enumeration (git add ... git apply) is present in all 39 agent files. 17 of those agent files had carried a stray U+000B control character in the rule block; the stray characters were removed and a post-change scan for C0 control characters across .github now returns 0 matches. Idempotency checked: grep of .github/ai-learning/learning-log.jsonl for 'mutating git|git rule|READ-ONLY INSPECTION|MUTATION BANNED' returned 0 matches before this append, so no prior record of this gap existed to update.
followup_action: none

description: A determinism assertion is only acceptable if it is mutation-proven or hand-computed; re-deriving with production code is a tautology
evidence: A Tier-3 determinism-reviewer flagged that the reserved-bleacher-slot assertion re-derived the expected value with the SAME algorithm production uses, so it could never fail. A second attempt was also tautological: a tripwire that re-derived the ring band sizes LOCALLY (from the same 0.25 split as production) did not fail under a production mutation of that split to 0.3. Remedy now in the repo: the tripwire was rewritten to READ THE BAND SIZES BACK FROM THE PRODUCTION EMISSION (examples/neatRacing/track/right-world.builder.test.ts:1539 'derives the reachable ring configuration from the track generator' - 'the inner/outer band sizes are read back from the emitted props, not re-derived here'), after which the same mutation failed the test.
followup_action: A new determinism or correctness assertion must be proven falsifiable by an independent means: a HAND-COMPUTED expected value, or a MUTATION PROBE against production. Any assertion whose expected value is produced by re-running the production algorithm (even inside the test) is a tautology and provides zero detection power. Apply this rule to every new contract in Step 14J and require the reviewer to name the falsification method before accepting an assertion.

description: Reason about a randomisation contract in terms of the POSITION of the reserved slot, not merely the COUNT of draws
evidence: The B5 contract requires a one-shot bleacher reservation to consume the same number of PRNG draws as the unreserved path. The original rationale claimed a skipped draw would shift 'every downstream prop'. Measured: the track generator emits 6..8 spline segments of 18 samples, so the reachable sample counts are 108/126/144, the ring slot counts are (2,8)/(3,9)/(3,11), and the reservation always lands on the TERMINAL outer slot (7/8/10). A skipped draw there has NO later prop to shift, so the rationale was vacuous in the reachable space and the only observable difference was the reserved bleacher's own colour draw (probabilistic 255/256). Remedy now in the repo: the ring emission closure was EXTRACTED into an EXPORTED production seam (emitRightWorldRing, examples/neatRacing/track/right-world.builder.ts:350 - 'exported so the stream contract can be exercised with a reserved slot that is NOT the terminal outer slot') and examples/neatRacing/track/right-world.builder.test.ts:1469 'keeps the stream stable when the reserved slot is not the terminal outer slot' drives a NON-TERMINAL reservation where a skipped draw shifts every later slot deterministically, with a negative control (expect(shifted).not.toEqual(production)) proving the comparison discriminates.
followup_action: Before using 'downstream drift' as the detection mechanism for a stream-preservation contract, measure the REACHABLE configuration space. If the affected element is always terminal, the drift signal is vacuous and the contract must be exercised through a seam that places it non-terminal; reserve an exported production seam for that purpose instead of duplicating the logic in a test.

description: A leftmost-lazy regex over a repeated plan section silently reads the wrong record
evidence: scripts/agent-customization/gates/specialist-review.gate.mjs matched the validation-evidence region with /VALIDATION_EVIDENCE[\s\S]*?(?=##|PlanUpdate|$)/i, which is a LEFTMOST match, so on a long multi-step plan it read only the FIRST evidence block (belonging to a CLOSED step) and reported 'no specialist review evidence found' for a step that HAD been reviewed. Fixed by unioning ALL regions with matchAll + the global flag (scripts/agent-customization/gates/specialist-review.gate.mjs: content.matchAll(/VALIDATION_EVIDENCE[\s\S]*?(?=##|PlanUpdate|$)/gi)), plus a regression test (scripts/agent-customization/gates/specialist-review.gate.test.mjs:200 'scans every validation-evidence region, not only the first one').
followup_action: When a gate scans a repeating section of a long document, a leftmost-match regex selects the FIRST record, not the ACTIVE one. Union all candidate regions and add a regression fixture with more than one record.

description: A stale Cortex/RAG index silently degrades the Cortex-First slice context that the implementer is told to load
evidence: The cortex-index gate FAILS for this plan (index_fresh: false): the RAG index still covers the DELETED examples/neatRacing/track/mechanic.sprite.test.ts and the pre-retirement right-world sources. neataptic-workflow-mcp-get_slice_context for P1-crowd-retire-people therefore returned an EMPTY acceptance-criteria list and a context block describing the OLD neatenstein-public + mechanic atlas merge - the authoritative contract the implementer is supposed to load was both EMPTY and WRONG, and the slice had to be executed from on-disk plan reads instead. The dispatched determinism-reviewer hit the same staleness independently and had to fall back to on-disk reads (its N4 finding).
followup_action: Treat get_slice_context as a CACHE, not as the authority: run the cortex-index gate BEFORE trusting the context payload, and fall back to on-disk plan reads whenever the acceptance-criteria list is empty or the context mentions constructs the slice retires. After a slice that DELETES or renames indexed files, rebuild the index (node rag-index/build-index.mjs) before the next slice relies on Cortex search.

description: TOOLING GAP (root-caused and verified 2026-10-27): normalizeTestContracts only reads criterion.text and criterion.id, so a STEP-level acceptance_criteria list authored as PLAIN STRINGS is normalized to empty contracts ({ id: '', text: '', validation: undefined }). The compact neataptic-workflow-mcp-get_slice_context payload therefore renders the step-level ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA block as EMPTY and the synthesized instructions string literally contains 'ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:' followed by empty bullets. SLICE-level acceptance criteria (authored as objects with id: and text:) render correctly, so a slice-level dispatch (both 14Q and 14Q2 dispatch via pre_execute_hook -> slice_id) receives a fully populated contract. Scope: the STEP-level render is broken, the SLICE-level render is correct.
evidence: Root cause: scripts/agent-customization/customization-utils.mjs normalizeTestContracts (around line 499) computes const text = String(criterion.text ?? '') and const explicitId = String(criterion.id ?? '').trim(); a plain STRING criterion has no .text or .id property, so text becomes '' and the AC-nnn id extraction has no source text, yielding { id: '', text: '', validation: undefined }. First observed 2026-10-22 while authoring Step 14K: the get_slice_context payload for P1-crowd2-red-contracts printed the heading ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: followed by six empty bullets, and converting the 14K criteria to the object form (- id: / text: / validation:) restored RED-A through RED-F with a populated instructions block. Root-caused and verified 2026-10-27 by the 01-planning VERIFICATION instance of the Step 14Q/14Q2 split in plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md: the STEP-level acceptance_criteria (lines 3226-3228) are plain strings ('- AC-088 (the seam carries the published severity): ...') while the SLICE-level acceptance_criteria (lines 3238-3242) are objects with id: and text:, and the step-level get_slice_context payload rendered 'ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:' plus three empty bullets. Correction of a prior claim: VERIFICATION 5 (2026-10-27) recorded this symptom as 'a RENDERING artifact of the compact context and NOT a defect' without root-causing it; the precise statement is that the STEP-level render drops string-form ACs while the SLICE-level render is correct, so this is a real defect in normalizeTestContracts, not a rendering artifact.
followup_action: Normalize string-form acceptance criteria inside normalizeTestContracts: when a criterion is a string, map it to { id: <AC-nnn extracted from the string via the AC-nnn pattern>, text: <the string>, validation: undefined } instead of String(criterion.text ?? ''). Interim mitigation: author every step-packet acceptance criterion in the object form (- id: AC-xxx / text: <full sentence> / validation: <command or check>) and treat a blank-bullet ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA block in get_slice_context as a hard signal to re-read the plan on disk; a remediation sweep should convert the remaining flat-string packets (14J, 14Q, 14Q2 and older).

description: Step 14K slice P1-crowd2-seat-density declares a 3-file boundary (right-world.builder.ts + right-world.builder.test.ts + public.sprite.ts) but its own red_test requires the RED-C POPULATION half to turn green ('every one of the 20 bleachers hosts seated billboards in the assembled scene at every fixture seed'), and the single-host restriction that made that assertion red lived OUTSIDE the boundary in filterBillboardsByCrowdHost (examples/neatRacing/track/right-world.pass.ts) - a file owned by the LATER slice P1-crowd2-off-bleacher-people (AC-074 crowd filter). No in-boundary-only edit could satisfy the slice's declared red_test, so the implementer was forced into a deliberate out-of-boundary edit that the plan records as a 'BOUNDARY DEVIATION (deliberate, documented, unavoidable)'.
evidence: plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md: (a) the Step 14K slice packet P1-crowd2-seat-density (lines 1718-1790) declares files_to_change = [right-world.builder.ts, right-world.builder.test.ts, public.sprite.ts] while its red_test lists 'RED-C (population half) turns green: every one of the 20 bleachers hosts seated billboards in the assembled scene at every fixture seed'; (b) the owning slice P1-crowd2-off-bleacher-people (from line 1804) holds AC-074 (crowd filter) 'filterBillboardsByCrowdHost stops dropping the non-host bleachers and the off-bleacher agents' yet claims only 'RED-C (off-bleacher half) turns green'; (c) line 6343 records the deviation verbatim: 'the single-host restriction that kept only ONE bleacher populated lived OUT of the boundary in filterBillboardsByCrowdHost (right-world.pass.ts), so NO in-boundary-only edit could turn the RED-C population half green ... The MINIMAL out-of-boundary pass edit was therefore made directly by 04 (3 edits)' - the in-boundary lever (making selectBleacherHostProp return undefined) would have broken the currently-green RED-B tests at right-world.builder.test.ts:1894 and :1912, and findHostProp is still live for filterBillboardsByAnchoringCapacity (right-world.pass.ts:301); (d) the slice note adds that 'the orchestrator and the plan owner MUST acknowledge it, and the next slice AC-074 no-deferred-cleanup clause MUST be amended before P1-crowd2-off-bleacher-people starts'. On disk the deviation is visible: filterBillboardsByCrowdHost (right-world.pass.ts:351) now returns only the non-walker billboards, with a doc comment stating that 'crowd host no longer owns the crowd, so every bleacher of the ring keeps the seated spectators it hosts and the assembled scene populates the WHOLE ring instead of a single stand', and the RED-C population assertion at right-world.pass.test.ts:1311 ('populates every bleacher of the scene with seated billboards at every fixture seed') is the contract that the out-of-boundary edit turned green. The 14K slice order red-contracts -> bleacher-count -> seat-density -> off-bleacher-people -> green means the slice that must satisfy the population half runs BEFORE the slice that owns the seam.
followup_action: Repair the 14K slice packets so a declared red_test is always satisfiable inside its own files_to_change: (a) amend the P1-crowd2-off-bleacher-people AC-074 no-deferred-cleanup clause as the plan already requires, since the crowd-host filter change landed early in the seat-density slice, and (b) add examples/neatRacing/track/right-world.pass.ts to P1-crowd2-seat-density.files_to_change in the plan of record (or restate the seat-density red_test as the ALLOCATION-only contract and move the assembled-scene population assertion to the owning slice) so boundary and red_test agree. Systemic follow-up for 01-planning: add a boundary/red_test cross-check to the plan-slice-quality or slice-advancement gate that FAILS when a slice's red_test names a contract whose only production seam lives in a file outside that slice's files_to_change, so a boundary deviation is caught at packet-authoring time instead of surfacing at implementation time as an out-of-boundary edit. Agents must treat a required out-of-boundary edit as a plan defect to report (as was done here), never as a silent scope widening.

description: The file `edit` tool can report a successful replacement that never lands on disk, and it matches PARTIAL lines (a unique prefix of a line) rather than whole lines only, so batch line-level rewrites must be verified after every call.
evidence: While de-indenting the ~65-line PlanUpdate YAML block in plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md (slice P1-crowd2-off-bleacher-people, Step 14K), two single-line edits (the `tests_for_05:` key and the closing fence) returned success while the file bytes were unchanged; re-applying the same intent with a 2-line chained anchor and with a bare-fence anchor landed correctly. An `old_str` that ended at EOF without a trailing newline failed to match at all. The same tool accepted partial-line prefix anchors, which is what made a cheap per-line de-indentation of the whole block possible.
followup_action: Never treat an `edit` success message as proof of a write: after a batch of edits, re-read the target range or count the new pattern with grep before recording validation evidence. Pre-check every candidate `old_str` for uniqueness with a regex count over the target file, prefer a 2-line chained anchor over a single full-line anchor, and include the trailing newline in end-of-file anchors.

description: JSDoc for the voxel-racer billboard/hosting filters must name the OPERATION the helper performs (drop vs move vs re-host) and must state which collections it does NOT touch, because prose that overstates the effect becomes a review finding.
evidence: Two of the five specialist-review rounds on slice P1-crowd2-off-bleacher-people failed on documentation accuracy alone: N15 (the personal-space pass was documented as having 'moved' billboards onto another host, but filterBillboardsByAnchoringCapacity only DROPS hosted billboards and never re-hosts them) and N18 (the same filter was documented as 'thinning the props', but the prop list and the MAX_PROPS LOD are untouched - only the hosted billboards are dropped). Both fixes were doc-only yet still forced a full focused-lane re-run (2 suites / 66 tests) and a fresh APPROVE round.
followup_action: When writing or editing a JSDoc for a selection/filter helper under examples/neatRacing/track, use the verb that matches the implementation (drop / keep / select) and state explicitly which collections are unaffected (props, LOD budgets, anchors). Reviewers of that pipeline should treat a prose/code verb mismatch as blocking, and the implementer should re-read its own new JSDoc once the code settles.

description: The green-light detection in step-packet.gate.mjs and plan-readiness.gate.mjs is not anchored on a stable marker: step-packet uses a multiline regex that captures ONLY the first body line of ## Latest validation evidence, and plan-readiness (same pattern without the multiline flag) passed on a FALSE POSITIVE because the old first bullet was an authoring note containing the literal substring 'green-light: true' inside a negated sentence ('does NOT record green-light: true').
evidence: Diagnosed during the P1-crowd2-green validation (Step 14K, 2026-10-23): before the evidence reword, plan-readiness reported greenLightFound true while the real Step 14K green light sat several entries down the section; the 05-green-testing agent reworded the first evidence bullet to a genuine green marker and re-ran both gates, yielding step-packet pass true and plan-readiness pass true / greenLightFound true as TRUE positives. Both gates are first-match substring scans over free-form prose, so any bullet containing the phrase (even negated) satisfies them.
followup_action: Repair both gates to anchor green-light detection on a dedicated stable marker (e.g. a literal 'green-light: true' line or an explicit marker bullet convention pinned at the top of ## Latest validation evidence), and add a negative fixture whose first body line contains the phrase inside a negation so the false positive cannot regress. Until repaired, treat plan-readiness greenLightFound as unverified without a read of the matched evidence line.

description: rag-index/build-index.mjs and embed-index.mjs treat --files= as a REPEATABLE flag: a single comma-separated value (e.g. --files=a.md,b.md) silently matches 0 files, exits 0, and reports a false-success reindex; one --files flag per file is required.
evidence: During the Step 14K green closure reindex (2026-10-23) a comma-separated --files value reported success with 0 files scanned/indexed while the plan family was not actually refreshed; re-running with one --files flag per file scanned 3 / indexed 1 / 363 chunks, and cortex-index then reported index_fresh true on the final bytes.
followup_action: Make build-index/embed-index reject a multi-path comma value in --files (or split it), and fail loudly when --files is provided but 0 files match, so a silent no-op reindex can never be recorded as a fresh index. Agents doing partial reindexes must pass one --files per file and verify scanned > 0.

description: neataptic-validation-mcp run_allowlisted_validation rejects allow-listed validation commands whose quoted argument contains the | shell metacharacter (e.g. the focused jest lane --testPathPatterns="examples/neatRacing/track|examples/neatRacing/engine"), so | alternation lanes cannot be executed through the validation-MCP relay and must be run directly via PowerShell.
evidence: During the P1-sprite-scale-green validation (Step 14L, 2026-10-23) the allow-listed npm run jest:base -- --testPathPatterns="examples/neatRacing/track|examples/neatRacing/engine" command was rejected by run_allowlisted_validation on the | metacharacter; the identical command executed directly via PowerShell ran the full 16-suite lane (409/410 tests, sole failure = pre-existing road-edge.test.ts:465 Step 14I debt), and the same caution was re-surfaced by the 03-red-testing and 04-implementing instances of Step 14L.
followup_action: Teach run_allowlisted_validation that | inside a quoted jest --testPathPatterns value is a regex alternation, not shell piping (permit it or escape it), or plan packets should split the lane into allow-list-safe entries; until repaired, agents run | lanes via PowerShell directly (documented worktree caution).

description: The Step 14L packet prose yields 4 backticked validation-command tokens against only 3 YAML validation entries, so the plan-command-lint consistency field reports validationCommandsMatch false - a packet-text mismatch (one prose command is not mirrored in the YAML allow-list), not a validation failure; the consolidated gate still passed 4/4.
evidence: During the P1-sprite-scale-green validation (Step 14L, 2026-10-23) the step packet prose enumerated 4 backticked command tokens while its YAML validation list carried 3 entries; slice-advancement passed (failedGates [], erroredGates []) but the detailed consistency check reported validationCommandsMatch false.
followup_action: Fold the missing prose command token into the Step 14L YAML validation list (or drop the prose token) in the next plan amendment; 01-planning must keep prose command tokens and YAML validation entries 1:1 when authoring step packets, and plan-command-lint should fail loudly on a token/entry count mismatch instead of only annotating it.

description: ts.readConfigFile(path) called WITHOUT the second ts.sys.readFile argument silently returns an undefined config, so ts.parseJsonConfigFileContent(...) yields EMPTY compiler options; a verification matrix built on those empty options matches NOTHING, even for files that are byte-identical under the correct options. Always pass the readFile callback, and prove any JSDoc/comment-only documentation pass behaviour-neutral with TWO independent, comment-insensitive TypeScript compiler-API fingerprints: (1) the SHA-256 of ts.transpileModule(src, { removeComments: true, compilerOptions: <repo tsconfig options> }).outputText, and (2) the raw character length of ts.createPrinter({ removeComments: true }).printFile(sf) - each PROVEN comment-insensitive first, by injecting a JSDoc block and a plain line comment into a copy and confirming the fingerprint does not move. Measure 2 is stronger than measure 1 because the printer AST print normalises string-literal quote style, which the emitter preserves.
evidence: During the Step 14K docs-quality closure pass (2026-10-23) the four-source-file behaviour-verification matrix was first run with ts.readConfigFile(path) (no readFile argument), which returned an undefined config; ts.parseJsonConfigFileContent then produced EMPTY compiler options, and the resulting transpile digest matched NO recorded pre-edit digest for ANY of the four changed source files, including the two that were byte-identical under the correct options. Had that matrix been trusted, the closure would have wrongly reported that all four changed source files had changed behaviour. The matrix was invalidated and re-run with the correct ts.readConfigFile(path, ts.sys.readFile) options, after which two of the four files reproduced their recorded pre-edit digests EXACTLY, confirming the documentation-only pass was behaviour-neutral. Both fingerprints were each proven comment-insensitive (a JSDoc block and a plain line comment injected into a copy; the fingerprint did not move) before being trusted.
followup_action: Always call ts.readConfigFile(path, ts.sys.readFile) and ASSERT the parsed config options are non-empty before using them; an empty or undefined options object is the signature of the missing readFile callback, and a fingerprint matrix that matches nothing is a defect in the matrix, never evidence of behaviour change. For any JSDoc/comment-only edit, use the two independent comment-insensitive compiler-API fingerprints (removeComments:true transpile SHA-256 plus removeComments:true printer printFile character length), prove each is comment-insensitive by comment injection before trusting it, prefer the printer length as the stronger measure because the emitter preserves string-literal quote style while the printer AST normalises it, and never conclude behaviour changed from a single fingerprint - require agreement of two independent measures plus exact reproduction of the pre-edit digest for files that are unchanged.

description: The neataptic-gate-mcp run_gate_check relay for the consolidated 'slice-advancement' gate can fail with 'did not return valid JSON' (empty stderr) even when the gate itself PASSES, because the MCP relay's outer spawn budget (GATE_SPAWN_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000) is not larger than the gate's own per-sub-gate budget (120_000) while the 7 sub-gates run SEQUENTIALLY. The sanctioned workaround is to run the SAME consolidated gate script directly with node and identical arguments (never the sub-gates individually).
evidence: MCP relay, REPRODUCED LIVE 2026-10-23 on slice P1-sprite-scale-world-factor: neataptic-gate-mcp:run_gate_check {gate: slice-advancement, args: {slice-id: P1-sprite-scale-world-factor, changed-files: examples/neatRacing/track/public.sprite.ts,examples/neatRacing/track/public.sprite.test.ts,examples/neatRacing/track/right-world.test.ts, plan: plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md}} -> {"error":"Gate 'slice-advancement' did not return valid JSON. stderr: "} (empty stderr, NO structured gate contract, so the caller cannot tell a tooling failure from a content failure). DIRECT invocation with the IDENTICAL arguments, recorded by the implementing instance in plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md '## Latest validation evidence' gate_evidence for Step 14L: node scripts/agent-customization/gates/slice-advancement.gate.mjs --json --slice-id=P1-sprite-scale-world-factor --changed-files=examples/neatRacing/track/public.sprite.ts,examples/neatRacing/track/public.sprite.test.ts,examples/neatRacing/track/right-world.test.ts --plan=plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md -> pass: true (severity FULL, specialistCount 1, failedGates []); 6 of 7 sub-gates green (plan-sync, step-packet, plan-slice-quality, plan-command-lint, code-coverage, specialist-review) and shared-validation reported gate_error 'spawnSync node ETIMEDOUT' - a TOOLING timeout on an execution-time gate, skipped by the gate's graceful-degradation design, NOT a content failure. Root cause: scripts/agent-customization/mcp/neataptic-gate-mcp.mjs:55 sets GATE_SPAWN_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000 as the OUTER budget for the consolidated gate, while scripts/agent-customization/gates/slice-advancement.gate.mjs:127 gives EVERY sub-gate its own 120_000 ms budget and the sub-gates are executed SEQUENTIALLY (slice-advancement.gate.mjs:227, gatesToRun.map over execFileSync), so at FULL severity the consolidated run routinely exceeds the 120 s outer budget; the killed spawn yields empty stdout, JSON.parse throws, and the relay hard-throws a STRING instead of a gate_error-classified contract. Recurrence of the SAME gap family: learn-20260929-104018-p1s4g2-gatemcp (2026-09-29, slice P1-S4-G2, 3x 'did not return valid JSON' with empty stderr while the direct runner returned PASS 4/4 TRIVIAL) and plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md:3833 defect (2), which diagnoses the identical defect (MCP outer budget deliberately EQUAL to the inner one, so the MCP path fails HARDER than the direct path).
followup_action: When run_gate_check returns 'did not return valid JSON' with empty stderr for slice-advancement, do NOT read it as a gate/content failure and do NOT run the sub-gates individually: re-run the SAME consolidated gate directly - node scripts/agent-customization/gates/slice-advancement.gate.mjs --json --slice-id=<slice> --changed-files=<csv> --plan=<plan> - and record THAT output as the gate evidence (plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md:7217 precedent). Remediation belongs in a dedicated agent-maintenance batch, NOT inside an implementation slice: replace the single flat GATE_SPAWN_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000 in scripts/agent-customization/mcp/neataptic-gate-mcp.mjs:55 with a PER-GATE outer budget (slice-advancement >= 1_800_000 ms because its sub-gates run SEQUENTIALLY; the four trivial plan gates stay short), add an explicit maxBuffer (>= 16 MiB), and on a spawn timeout / empty stdout return a gate_error-classified structured contract {pass, gate_error: true, spawned error/status/signal/stdout byte length} instead of throwing a string, so a tooling failure can never be recorded as a content failure. The gate still has NO regression test file (scripts/agent-customization/gates/slice-advancement.gate.test.mjs does not exist), so add one covering the per-gate budget map, the timeout-is-not-a-content-failure distinction and the content-failure guard.

description: The Step 14L slice P1-sprite-scale-world-factor orchestrator_note asserted a FACTUALLY WRONG intermediate state: because the right-world pass keeps its own copy of the meters-per-pixel constant, 'the rendered quad is still 9.6 m tall at the end of this slice and only the placement footprint is halved'. The claim mistook a duplicated CONSTANT for a duplicated LEVER - right-world.pass.ts:919-920 computes the uploaded quad scale as computeBillboardScale(distance) * NEATRACING_BILLBOARD_WORLD_PIXEL_SCALE, a PRODUCT that already contains the shared world-scale lever, so flipping NEATRACING_PUBLIC_BILLBOARD_WORLD_SCALE = 0.5 in public.sprite.ts already halves the RENDERED quad with right-world.pass.ts byte-IDENTICAL. The plan was corrected IN PLACE with a dated marker, and the next slice P1-sprite-scale-render-quad must not be scoped on the premise that the halving is still pending.
evidence: DEFECT: plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md:1980 (the P1-sprite-scale-world-factor slice packet orchestrator_note) stated 'the pass keeps its own copy of the meters-per-pixel constant until the next slice, so the rendered quad is still 9.6 m tall at the end of this slice and only the placement footprint is halved. That temporary state is intentional'. The premise is false. (1) THE CALL GRAPH: right-world.pass.ts:107 declares NEATRACING_BILLBOARD_WORLD_PIXEL_SCALE = 0.05, a byte-for-byte copy of the shared NEATRACING_BILLBOARD_WORLD_PIXEL_SCALE_M = 0.05 (public.sprite.ts:413) - it duplicates only the meters-per-pixel FACTOR (0.05 m/px), never the world-scale LEVER. right-world.pass.ts:919-920 builds the quad scale as 'const scale = computeBillboardScale(distance) * NEATRACING_BILLBOARD_WORLD_PIXEL_SCALE', and computeBillboardScale (public.sprite.ts:732-739) returns the NAMED lever NEATRACING_PUBLIC_BILLBOARD_WORLD_SCALE = 0.5 (public.sprite.ts:440) for every distance - so the lever is ALREADY a multiplicand of the rendered quad and the duplicate twin cannot hold the quad at 9.6 m. (2) THE MEASUREMENT: the RED-C contract in right-world.pass.test.ts (docblock :41-46, assertions :2378-2382 and :2412-2416) measures the uploaded vertex quad at frame.height x 0.5 x 0.05 = 4.8 m full height and frame.width x 0.5 x 0.05 / 2 = 2.4 m half width; the focused lane moved from right-world.pass.test.ts 2 failed / 36 passed / 38 (exit 1) at RED (plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md:7170) to 38/38 (exit 0) at GREEN, i.e. RED-C and RED-D turned green WITHOUT any pass-file edit. description: Three reusable Puppeteer/WebGL harness gaps plus one latent quadratic fixture hot spot were measured while repairing the visible-foreground drift smoke fixture, and together they make a browser-validation slice fail for reasons that live in the HARNESS rather than in the code under test, or hang with a message that points at the wrong cause: (1) page.setContent() does NOT re-run page.evaluateOnNewDocument() hooks, so the WebGL interception never installs and the harness reports 'no data captured' instead of 'the hook did not install' - a silent false-negative generator; (2) the default Puppeteer protocolTimeout of 180 s is shorter than a legitimately long fixture run and its failure text ('Runtime.callFunctionOn timed out') is indistinguishable from a hung page, when the real cause was a busy renderer main thread; (3) a backgrounded or occluded window throttles requestAnimationFrame, so the fixture can silently never progress and the run only advances when the window is genuinely visible AND in the foreground; and (4) the fixture itself carried an O(greenPoints x roadPoints) brute-force nearest-road scan that was unreachable behind the earlier staleness failure and only became reachable after the repair, where it blocked the renderer main thread for minutes. The consequence is that a browser smoke can be declared broken (or hung) for harness reasons, and a fixture that was previously 'not reached' can hide a quadratic main-thread hot spot.
evidence: (1) setContent vs evaluateOnNewDocument: the WebGL interception is installed through page.evaluateOnNewDocument(...); under page.setContent(html) the hook NEVER ran - the probe proved it because the expected injected globals __p1ctxCount and __p1frames were ABSENT from the page context, the fixture captured no buffer upload at all and every probe reported 'failed to capture the VBO'; the identical page content served through page.goto(url) DID run the hook and the injection keys appeared. (2) protocolTimeout: the first visible-window run died with 'Runtime.callFunctionOn timed out' (a 180 s waitForFunction timeout) which looks exactly like a hung page, but the renderer main thread was merely busy (see (4)); protocolTimeout: 900000 is required for this fixture class. (3) foreground requirements: the render only advanced when the window was genuinely visible AND in the foreground; the working combination on this host was page.goto() (not setContent), the Chrome flags --disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows --disable-renderer-backgrounding --disable-background-timer-throttling --disable-features=CalculateNativeWinOcclusion, page.bringToFront(), and a Win32 foreground-activation helper (SetForegroundWindow / BringWindowToTop / ShowWindow applied to the Chrome window whose command line contains the test --user-data-dir), applied repeatedly during the run; a separate --user-data-dir outside the repo is required while the developer's own Chrome is running; and a page.setContent() page must receive the fixture CSS or the canvas is 0x0 and nothing renders. (4) the O(n^2) fixture hot spot: the fixture measured the distance from every coloured track vertex to the nearest road point with a brute-force O(greenPoints x roadPoints) scan over 603,300 road points; measured 147 ms for 201 green points, i.e. an extrapolated ~170 s for the three band means, which is what blocked the renderer main thread in (2); the repair replaced it with an EXACT uniform-grid nearest-road search (4 m cells, expanding ring, a proven-exact termination bound plus an exhaustive fallback) whose result is IDENTICAL - 300 sampled green points, 0 mismatches against the brute force, maxDiff 0 - at ~1,100 ms instead of ~170 s. Also measured: the same fixture class silently dropped undefined-valued check keys through JSON.stringify, which is why ten road-edge checks were invisible in the serialized result of the earlier NOT OK verdict; and the repaired fixture now reports window.p1TurnDriftGreenSmokeResult.passed === true with all 31 checks true, reproduced across TWO captured runs (9,831 ms and 10,506 ms) in a NON-HEADLESS visible foreground Chrome 155.0.8059.85 window with 0 fixture console errors.
followup_action: (a) DONE inside this slice (fixture-only, one file: docs/browser-tests/scenarios/p1-turn-drift-green-smoke.html): the O(n^2) nearest-road scan is replaced by the exact uniform-grid search (ROAD_GRID_CELL_M = 4, expanding ring, proven-exact termination bound, exhaustive fallback) with IDENTICAL results at ~1,100 ms instead of ~170 s; the singlePlanePaint measurement is now taken on the paint plane only (PAINT_Y_THRESHOLD) so the 37,452-vertex ground slab at y = -0.5 is no longer counted as paint; the three enumerated staleness defects (track program marker, 7-float track VBO stride, wheel VBO selection by measured identity) are closed; and the fixture now reports passed === true with all 31 checks true in a visible foreground window (two captured runs, 9,831 ms and 10,506 ms, Chrome 155.0.8059.85, 0 console errors). NO harness-level fix landed - the remediation in (b) is still open. (b) REMAINING for agent-maintenance-coordinator with browser-harness-specialist and browser-ui-specialist: land ONE reusable visible-foreground smoke harness contract in .github/skills/browser-testing-harness/SKILL.md and the browser-harness-specialist agent that states: (i) navigate with page.goto(url) and NEVER page.setContent() when the scenario depends on a page.evaluateOnNewDocument(...) injection, AND assert the injected globals (__p1ctxCount / __p1frames) are present BEFORE consuming capture data, so a missing hook is reported as 'the hook did not install' and never as 'no data captured'; (ii) an explicit long protocolTimeout (900000 ms) for this fixture class, with the timeout error path stating 'the renderer main thread may be busy - distinguish it from a hang' and, on a protocol timeout, re-checking main-thread liveness before reporting a hang; (iii) the anti-throttling launch contract - the four Chrome flags --disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows --disable-renderer-backgrounding --disable-background-timer-throttling --disable-features=CalculateNativeWinOcclusion, page.bringToFront(), a Win32 foreground-activation helper (SetForegroundWindow / BringWindowToTop / ShowWindow on the Chrome window whose command line contains the test --user-data-dir) applied repeatedly during the run, a separate --user-data-dir outside the repo while the developer's own Chrome is running, and the fixture CSS delivered to any setContent page so the canvas is not 0x0; (iv) a fixture-level serialization rule that a check with an undefined value is emitted explicitly (e.g. null plus a named reason) instead of being dropped by JSON.stringify, so missing checks cannot hide behind a shorter result object. (c) REMAINING for 04-implementing / 05-green-testing: before any browser smoke is trusted as green, re-profile the fixture for quadratic main-thread hot spots (a fixture that was unreachable behind an earlier failure can hide one) and diagnose a protocol timeout as 'the main thread is busy' before diagnosing it as 'the page is hung'.

description: The devtools MCP facade cannot ATTACH to an already-running visible Chrome: scripts/agent-customization/mcp/devtools-facade.mjs DEFAULT_SPAWN_COMMAND (line 44) spawns 'npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@1.6.0 --headless=false --usage-statistics=false --performance-crux=false --allow-unrestricted-paths=true' with NO attach flag (no --browserUrl and no CDP endpoint), so the spawned MCP always LAUNCHES ITS OWN Chrome under its own managed profile instead of reusing the visible foreground instance already serving CDP on port 9222. The facade docblock (lines 27-42) and the chrome-devtools-mcp / devtools skills still promise the opposite ('the MCP will reuse it when it can attach to the remote debugging port' / 'the DevTools MCP can attach to that existing browser instance instead of launching a new one'), so the documented contract is unimplementable through the facade, and the visible-foreground browser validation has to be driven over RAW CDP (manual 'Start-Process chrome.exe --remote-debugging-port=9222' + 'puppeteer-core connect({browserURL})') - a surface outside the browser specialists' declared tool allowlist (devtools/devtools + execute).

(2) launchVisibleChrome does not close the loop either: devtools-facade.mjs:98-133 only spawns Chrome and returns {pid, port, url, args} - it never returns or forwards a browserUrl to the MCP - and it builds an UNQUOTED shell command (spawn with shell: isWin at devtools-facade.mjs:122), so an executable path containing spaces fails silently. (4) The 2026-10-24 05-green-testing FINAL re-verification of Step 14G / P1-arcade-drift-green (plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md:2281 and :3828) records the visible-window smoke as 'delegated to the Tier-3 browser-ui-specialist, attached over raw CDP to a REAL VISIBLE FOREGROUND Chrome 155.0.8059.85 window' with 'CDP 9222, user-data-dir C:\temp\chrome-p1drift' - i.e. the sanctioned devtools MCP surface (take_screenshot / evaluate_script / performance_start_trace) was NOT the surface that produced the green evidence, because that surface cannot attach to the visible window. description: A DEAD legacy read path inside a browser fixture is a LATENT SILENT-DEGRADATION hazard the moment a field is added to the seam it reads. The 14N W3 fixture's readDriftSeam() USED TO read window.neatRacingDebug.drift FIRST - an identifier written NOWHERE in the repo - so if that old 4-field shape had ever been reintroduced it would have been read INSTEAD of the five-field seam, tick would have been undefined, and the tick budgets would have silently degraded to frame budgets. The reusable rule: when a fixture reads a seam, read it from ONE place, and delete every dead or legacy branch on that read path IN THE SAME STEP that changes the seam's shape (No Deferred Cleanup) - a dead branch is not harmless code, it is a shape-selection branch that nothing exercises and everything depends on.
evidence: THE DEAD PATH (now removed): readDriftSeam() (docs/browser-tests/scenarios/p1-turn-drift-green-smoke.html:1266) used to read window.neatRacingDebug.drift first and only then window.neatRacingDriftState; neatRacingDebug is written NOWHERE in the repo - the plan's own record at plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md:9594 states 'the DEAD legacy seam branch (window.neatRacingDebug.drift, written NOWHERE in the repo) is REMOVED from the fixture's readDriftSeam() in the SAME step that introduced the fifth field - a re-introduced 4-field shape would have been read instead of the five-field seam, tick would have been undefined, and the tick budgets would have silently degraded to frame budgets', and the fixture's own comment block (:1258-1265) carries the same rationale. THE HAZARD CHAIN, all on-disk: (1) the production seam is EXACTLY five fields and is written per frame at examples/neatRacing/browser-entry/browser-entry.ts:980-986 (poseRad, slipAngleRad, speedMps, tickHz and tick = car.tick); (2) the fixture's sampleDriftSeam() (:1283-1307) is undefined-tolerant and yields tick: undefined for a 4-field shape; (3) feelCurrentTick() (:1126-1133) returns null when the seam reports no tick, and its own comment says 'every tick-addressed measurement degrades to a frame count'; (4) observeFeelPhase() (:1407, degraded branch :1483-1491) then completes the phase on a FRAME budget of the tick budget and flags it degraded; (5) the CAPTURE POINT is recorded only when NOT degraded (:1519), so the capture would be MISSING rather than wrong; (6) maxFeelPoseRateDegPerS() (:1664-1691) pairs only frames carrying a numeric, INCREASING tick, so with tick undefined it finds ZERO pairs, and the check driftFeelPoseRateBounded is written as 'poseRate.pairs > 0 && poseRate.maxRate <= DRIFT_FEEL_POSE_RATE_MAX_DEG_PER_S' (:2533-2534) - a NON-VACUITY WITNESS, so the check reports FALSE, never a vacuous pass. HONEST NUANCE (so this event is not misread as 'the fixture would have gone falsely green'): the fixture was NOT a silent-green machine - the degraded flag, the missing-capture guard and the pairs > 0 witness would each have turned the mis-read into a FAILED or MISSING-DATA result. The real cost of the dead branch was MISATTRIBUTION (the symptom reads as 'the tick budgets are broken' or 'the pose-rate check failed', not as 'the fixture read a dead 4-field seam shape') plus the risk that a frame-budget fallback produces plausible-looking phase durations; the same-step removal was still right, because the dead branch was a shape-selection branch no test exercised. THE REMOVAL: the branch is gone and the seam is read from ONE place, still defensively - a missing or throwing seam yields null and never aborts the fixture (:1266-1274).
followup_action: (a) When a browser fixture (or any consumer) reads a named seam, keep exactly ONE read path: any legacy or alternate shape branch is DEAD CODE and must be deleted in the same step that changes the seam's shape, never deferred - a deferred dead branch is a latent shape-selection branch that no test exercises. (b) When a seam gains a field, treat every reader of the OLD shape as a shape-consumer: audit each reader for an undefined-tolerant path (a missing field must become an explicit, REPORTED degradation, never a silent default) and keep a non-vacuity witness on every measurement that depends on the new field - the fixture's 'poseRate.pairs > 0' is the model, a measurement with zero samples reports FALSE, never true. (c) A seam is a RUNTIME contract, so a source-only change is not a change: the served artifact must be rebuilt and its identity (bytes + sha256) recorded, because a stale bundle silently serves the OLD shape - here the rebuild produced the five-field literal neatRacingDriftState={poseRad:...,slipAngleRad:...,speedMps:...,tickHz:...,tick:L.tick} in a 398,699-byte bundle (sha256 3C255A7F91A99AA8B3C7172B2BADCD23426DC63746A286E81778A16E33FFD9D8) for BOTH docs/assets/neatracing.bundle.js and examples/neatRacing/assets/neatracing.bundle.js. (d) For agent-maintenance-coordinator with browser-harness-specialist: add a lint that FAILS a browser fixture which reads a window.<debug> property that no production file ever writes (an unresolvable seam identifier), so the next dead branch is caught statically instead of by a rebase.

description: A mandated specialist co-sign on a multi-surface contract change converges in ROUNDS, and the productive pattern is to hand the reviewer the EXACT list of applied fixes with file:line anchors and ask for a CONFIRM-ONLY pass. The api-contract-reviewer co-sign for the Step 14N W3 five-field seam took 3 rounds (2 x REQUEST_CHANGES, then APPROVE), and round 2 existed only because round 1's fix list was itself INCOMPLETE - one live criterion was fixed while two sibling live rows were missed - because a reviewer can only confirm a change it can be shown. The dispatch contract reinforces the pattern: scripts/agent-customization/dispatch/build-dispatch-packet.mjs:18 sets PROMPT_LENGTH_MAX = 500 and resolvePromptLengthMax() returns 500 for moderate and complex slices (200 for trivial), so a dispatch prompt CANNOT inline a long fix list - the anchored brief must live in the RAG-indexed plan or artifact and the prompt must carry only the slice ID plus a compact anchor pointer.
evidence: THE CO-SIGN (recorded at plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md:9591-9592): 'the api-contract-reviewer co-sign (MANDATED by the W3 contract) took 3 rounds. Round 1 = REQUEST_CHANGES with 4 blocking findings: the live plan criterion (L2423) still mandated FOUR fields and the dated PATCH B-3 entry (L4003) said the seam must NOT grow a fifth; the fixture comment still said FIXED at four fields; BOTH shipped bundles still emitted the 4-field seam; the gate doc section 1 named the deleted car.driftYawOffset. Round 2 = REQUEST_CHANGES: the B-1 amendment was INCOMPLETE - the live RED-slice criterion (L2375) and the AC-087 row (L482) still said 4 fields, and the blocker-table B-3 row (L8984) asserted a now-false fact about L2423. Round 3 = APPROVE.' The same record then lists the applied fixes with their anchors: 'the live plan criteria (L2423, L2375), the AC-087 row (L482) and the blocker-table B-3 row (L8984) all state the FIVE-field seam; the dated PATCH B-3 entry's clause is WITHDRAWN by a dated SUPERSEDED bullet (L4004); the fixture comment and the gate doc section 1 were corrected; the bundle was rebuilt and the tracked copy refreshed.' THE DISPATCH BUDGET (read directly at capture time): scripts/agent-customization/dispatch/build-dispatch-packet.mjs:18 'export const PROMPT_LENGTH_MAX = 500;' with the docblock 'Prompts exceeding this limit are rejected to enforce RAG-based dispatch (short prompt + slice ID, not inline design context)'; :26 PROMPT_LENGTH_MAX_TRIVIAL = 200; :33 COMPLEXITY_LEVELS = ['trivial','moderate','complex']; :40 DEFAULT_COMPLEXITY = 'moderate'; :90-93 resolvePromptLengthMax() returns 200 for trivial and 500 otherwise; the MCP surface states the same contract at scripts/agent-customization/mcp/neataptic-dispatch-mcp.mjs:155-159 and :204-208 ('Trivial slices get a 200-character prompt limit; moderate/complex get 500'); the limit is enforced and REGRESSION-TESTED at scripts/agent-customization/dispatch/build-dispatch-packet.test.mjs:118-121 (resolvePromptLengthMax('moderate') === 500 and ('complex') === 500) and :215-267 (a 500-character prompt is accepted and a 501-character prompt is rejected with prompt_length_max 500, for both moderate and complex). THE LINK BETWEEN THE TWO FACTS IS MECHANICAL: with a 500-character cap the reviewer's brief cannot travel inside the dispatch prompt, so it must be anchored in the RAG-indexed plan - which is exactly where the reviewer read it, and exactly why the anchor list, not a prose narrative, is the artifact that makes a confirm-only pass possible.
followup_action: (a) PRODUCTIVE PATTERN, reusable for every mandated co-sign: before asking for a re-review, hand the reviewer the EXACT list of applied fixes as file:line anchors plus a one-line reason per anchor, and ask for a CONFIRM-ONLY pass ('confirm these N anchors, or return the specific anchor that is wrong'). This converts an open-ended re-read into a finite checklist and is what took the co-sign from a stalled round 2 to APPROVE in round 3. (b) The anchor list must come from a FULL enumeration of the affected rows BEFORE the first review - round 2 existed purely because the round-1 fix list was incomplete (L2375 and L482 were missed after L2423 was fixed), so the enumeration is the cheap preventive and the extra review rounds are the expensive symptom. (c) The 500-character dispatch budget is a FEATURE of RAG-based dispatch (short prompt + slice ID, not inline design context - build-dispatch-packet.mjs:13-18): put the brief in the RAG-indexed plan or artifact, keep the dispatch prompt to the slice ID plus a compact anchor pointer, and never try to inline a long fix list into the prompt - it will be rejected with prompt_length_max 500. (d) For agent-maintenance-coordinator: the builder has no field for a reviewer brief, so an anchored list currently has to be smuggled through the plan; consider an explicit review-brief field EXEMPT from the PROMPT_LENGTH_MAX check, so a co-sign can be dispatched with a machine-checked anchor list instead of a prose hand-off.

description: Tightening a GEOMETRIC BOUND silently invalidates the fixtures of every OTHER contract that was anchored to the old bound, not only the contracts that name the bound. The Step 14P slice P1-drift-rewire-road-surface moved the track-boundary containment bound from the outer grass-apron edge (halfWidth + NEATRACING_TRACK_GRASS_APRON_WIDTH_M) to the drivable-surface edge (the nearest segment driveable half width) to satisfy the AC-081 / AC-089 contract. Two contracts in the SAME test file that never mention the bound were anchored to it: the P0-3 / AC-079 drift-channel wipe contracts (a boundary bounce only fires OUTSIDE the bound, so the sliding fixture car must sit outside the NEW bound) and the closed Step P1-S7-C lat-5 interpretation pin (a car at lat 5 was byte-identical under the old bound and is now reseated onto the drivable edge). The reusable rule: when a bound, a threshold or a band edge moves, GREP THE WHOLE TEST SURFACE for every fixture anchored to that edge - not only the tests that name it - and record each re-anchored fixture as an explicit RE-BASELINE in the slice record; a fixture that is re-anchored silently is a contract that can rot without any failing assertion.
evidence: THE BOUND MOVE (recorded in the slice PlanUpdate at plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md, Step 14P / P1-drift-rewire-road-surface): resolveTrackBoundaryCar now reads the bound from nearestChord.halfWidthM (the outer edge of the road core plus the curb band) instead of halfWidth + NEATRACING_TRACK_GRASS_APRON_WIDTH_M, and the private reboundPastApronEdge was renamed reboundPastDrivableSurfaceEdge because the old name referenced the retired bound. THE SIBLING FIXTURE THAT HAD TO MOVE: the P0-3 drift-channel fixture (four it() blocks) seated its sliding car at outerApronBoundM + 1 (7.0 + 1); under the new bound that car is INSIDE the drivable surface, so NO bounce fires and the channel-wipe contracts would have failed - the fixture had to be re-anchored to drivableSurfaceEdgeM + 1. THE CLOSED-STEP PIN: the P1-S7-C red contract (recorded in plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.logs.md:2013 and confirmed by the plan at :818) had deliberately pinned the OUTER grass-apron bound with an untouched-at-lat-5 byte-identity assertion at ~88% confidence, and the closed step record at plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md:818-819 still describes that interpretation - the implementing slice must NOT rewrite the closed record, it must re-baseline the pin in its OWN record and let the later record supersede the earlier one. THE PROOF THAT THE COUPLING IS REAL (not theoretical): the bound was temporarily re-pointed at the retired outer-apron edge and the same targeted command reported 7 failed / 28 passed / 35 total - the failures were the three boundary contracts AND the four P0-3 drift-channel contracts, proving that a bound move reaches contracts that never name the bound. THE AUTHORISATION: the plan pre-authorised the case - the author decision D_Q8 states that if Step 14I has not landed the wave implements the SAME bound and Step 14I records the satisfaction, so the two steps never implement two different bounds - and the Step 14I P1-track-road-containment packet now carries that satisfaction_record.
followup_action: (a) When a bound, a threshold, a band edge or a magic offset moves, GREP the whole test surface for fixtures anchored to that edge before running anything: the failing-test count is NOT the discovery mechanism (a fixture re-anchored in the same edit hides the coupling), the grep is. (b) A fixture that must move because a BOUND moved is a RE-BASELINE, not a test fix: record it in the slice PlanUpdate with the old anchor, the new anchor and the reason, so the green slice can enter it in the shared re-baseline ledger instead of the change looking cosmetic. (c) When a later AC supersedes a pin recorded by a CLOSED step, do not rewrite the closed step record - the later slice record supersedes it explicitly and the closed step stays a true history. (d) The one-bound rule has a concrete guard: when two steps own the same bound, the second step records the SATISFACTION in the first step packet (satisfaction_record) and does NOT flip the first step status - the first step green slice owns the status and the served-page evidence. (e) For agent-maintenance-coordinator: a static helper that lists every test fixture constant derived from a bound (for example every FIXTURE_HALF_TRACK_WIDTH_M expression in a test file) would make the coupling greppable in one command.

description: RE-DERIVING a SHARED constant in an implementing slice invalidates the ratified literals of EVERY contract anchored to it, but the implementing slice owns only the SOURCE file - the re-baselined TEST literals usually belong to a LATER slice whose files_to_change cap may not even include the test files, so the re-baselining can end up OWNED BY NOBODY and the wave cannot close. The Step 14Q slice P1-drift-law-proportional re-derived the drift body yaw gain (0.5 -> 0.45) and the DECLARED pose envelope (0.3050 -> 0.30185 rad) in examples/neatRacing/physics/drift.model.ts. That single source change invalidated five ratified literals in THREE test files the slice does not own: the drift model suite (the anti-null gain pin expect(GAIN).toBe(0.5) and the proxy identity 0.04938855057460811), the service suite (the two envelope-derivation pins, the old committed-ceiling basis 0.225 and the pose 0.305) and the car pass suite (the DERIVED MAX_SLIP x GAIN pin 0.225). The green slice P1-drift-law-green owns the fixture html, the fixture-gate doc and the plan - NOT the test files - so as the packets stand nobody may re-pin them. The reusable rule: an implementing slice that re-derives a constant must GREP THE WHOLE TEST SURFACE for every literal anchored to it (the constant name AND its DERIVED products), REPORT one RE-BASELINE LEDGER ROW per literal (the old baseline, the new baseline, the MEASURED value and the OWNER FILE) in its own slice record, and escalate the OWNERSHIP question - the ledger row is the hand-off artifact, not an optional nicety. A second reusable rule from the same slice: a plan RECOMMENDED value can be INFEASIBLE under the ratified guards, and the implementing slice must record the INFEASIBILITY PROOF and the feasible window instead of silently choosing another number - the plan recommended a yaw gain of 0.75 while the ratified anti-null guard (|GAIN - 1| >= 0.5) forces GAIN <= 0.5 and the ratified 0.2 rad prominence floor forces |GAIN - 1| >= 0.4444, so 0.75 would have put the drift BELOW its own announcement floor; the feasible window was [0.386, 0.5] and 0.45 was chosen.
evidence: THE SOURCE CHANGE (examples/neatRacing/physics/drift.model.ts, the only file of the slice): NEATRACING_DRIFT_VISUAL_YAW_GAIN_RAD 0.5 -> 0.45 and NEATRACING_DRIFT_POSE_ENVELOPE_RAD 0.3050 -> 0.30185 rad, with the envelope re-derived from the MAXIMUM PUBLISHED ceiling (0.493 off-road) instead of the committed ceiling (0.45) because the pose spring is driven by the PUBLISHED slip in BOTH regimes. THE FIVE INVALIDATED LITERALS: (1) drift.model.test.ts [RED-7G-ANTI-NULL] expect(NEATRACING_DRIFT_VISUAL_YAW_GAIN_RAD).toBe(0.5) - the guard inside the same contract (|GAIN - 1| >= 0.5) still PASSES at 0.45; (2) drift.model.test.ts [RED-7C-PROXY] the identity 0.04938855057460811 -> 0.05432740563206893; (3) physics.step.service.test.ts [RED-7E-ENVELOPE-DERIVATION] the committed-ceiling basis 0.225 -> 0.2025; (4) physics.step.service.test.ts [RED-7E-ENVELOPE-DERIVATION-POSE] 0.305 -> 0.2825; (5) engine/passes/car.pass.test.ts the DERIVED MAX_SLIP x GAIN pin 0.225 -> 0.2025. description: PUBLISHING a NEW DERIVED field on a SHARED state record turns that record into a MULTI-OWNER contract, but a slice packet with a tight files_to_change cap only names the OWNER of the field - it never names the OTHER modules that RECONSTRUCT the same record. The Step 14Q slice P1-drift-traction-scalar published the new named field tractionSeverity on the PhysicsCarState record in examples/neatRacing/physics/physics.step.service.ts (the ONLY file of the slice; the law computeTractionSeverity already existed in examples/neatRacing/physics/drift.model.ts through the sibling slice P1-drift-law-proportional). A construction sweep showed that examples/neatRacing/physics/collision.utils.ts REBUILDS a car state by SPREADING the previous record on the collision bounce (the drift channel is zeroed and the published slip is set to 0), so a bounced state carries the PRE-BOUNCE tractionSeverity for exactly ONE published frame, until the next stepPhysics tick recomputes it from the zeroed slip. collision.utils.ts is NOT in the slice files_to_change, so the residual could only be REPORTED, not patched - and the sibling field travelHeadingRad (published by Step 14P) already has the SAME characteristic, because the bounce recompose keeps the pre-bounce travel heading too. The reusable rule: an implementing slice that adds a field to a shared state record MUST SWEEP EVERY MODULE THAT CONSTRUCTS OR RECOMPOSES that record (not only the modules that READ it), and the slice packet should carry an explicit acceptance criterion for that sweep, because the READ-side consumers are usually listed in the AC while the CONSTRUCT-side ones are not. The zero per-frame allocation rule was NOT broken: a primitive number field on the already-allocated per-tick record adds no allocation.
evidence: THE CHANGE (examples/neatRacing/physics/physics.step.service.ts, the only production file of the slice): the PhysicsCarState interface gained the named field tractionSeverity (number); the spawn record publishes tractionSeverity 0; the tick pipeline computes computeTractionSeverity(nextSlipAngle, nextSpeedAfterTraction) as the new step 6 and publishes it on the returned state, where nextSlipAngle is the very number published as state.slipAngle and nextSpeedAfterTraction is the very number published as state.speed (the POST-traction speed, after the drift scrub and the off-road floor). The law is the model export computeTractionSeverity (examples/neatRacing/physics/drift.model.ts) - the service PUBLISHES the law value, so no consumer can re-derive a different number. THE CONSTRUCTION SWEEP: the grep for PhysicsCarState over examples/neatRacing returned the reconstruction sites in physics/collision.utils.ts (the displaceCar, recomposeCarWithVelocity and reboundPastDrivableSurfaceEdge helpers), in host/race-session.ts and in the test suites - EVERY one of them builds a record by SPREADING a previous record, so the new REQUIRED field breaks no type contract (npx tsc -p tsconfig.neatRacing.json --noEmit exits 0). THE RESIDUAL: the collision bounce recompose (physics/collision.utils.ts, recomposeCarWithVelocity) overwrites speed, slipAngle, lateralVelocity and drift but NOT tractionSeverity, so a bounced car publishes the PRE-BOUNCE severity for one frame; the file is outside the slice cap, so the residual is reported in RISKS_OR_GAPS instead of patched. description: BACKGROUND-AGENT COMPLETION NOTIFICATIONS CAN BE LOST ACROSS CLI SESSION BOUNDARIES, and an orchestrator that treats no-notification as no-progress will sit idle for hours. During Step 14Q the slice P1-drift-traction-scalar (04-implementing, background agent 34f5a687) genuinely finished at about 2026-10-27T19:45Z: it wrote its structured-v1 report, went idle, appended its PlanUpdate to the plan and its learning event to the log. But the completion wake-up never reached the orchestrator turn loop across a CLI session boundary, so the orchestrator stayed idle for about 9 hours while the user observed that nothing was running, and a concurrently failed RAG re-index (SQLITE_BUSY: database is locked, exit 1) went unretried because the idle orchestrator never checked its background shells either. The queue stalled for the full window even though the work was DONE. The reusable rule: for a session orchestrator, the absence of a completion notification is an UNKNOWN STATE, never evidence of no progress - notifications are a convenience, not a contract.
evidence: THE INCIDENT: user message at about 2026-10-28T04:56Z reported NOTHING is running after hours of downtime; a list_agents cross-check showed agent 34f5a687 idle with 33548s elapsed and its full SUCCESS report unread (total_turns 1, the report was there the whole time), plus a separate correctly-scoped agent 82bbbbae (slice P1-drift-law-repin, agent 14N-K-impl-14Q-repin) already running under its own dispatch. Shell history showed the parallel RAG re-index (shellId 1395) had failed with SQLITE_BUSY exit 1 hours earlier and had never been retried. THE RECOVERY (under one hour): the unread structured-v1 report was read and reconciled, both slice statuses were flipped to DONE in the plan with embedded evidence, a NEW-TOP validation-evidence entry was appended, the SQLITE_BUSY re-index was retried successfully (scanned 2010, indexed 2, chunks 683; embed embedded 688, skipped 27476), and the queue resumed at the next boundary (P1-drift-law-code-green dispatch) with no work lost and no duplicate dispatched against a live agent. THE ROOT CAUSE: background-agent completion notifications are delivered by the runtime between turns; a session boundary / compaction between the notification and the next orchestrator turn dropped the wake-up, and no fallback existed. THE MITIGATION NOW STANDING (recorded in the plan validation evidence as a standing mitigation): an orchestrator MUST cross-check list_agents against its expected dispatch queue on EVERY turn and after every session boundary or compaction, MUST immediately read the structured-v1 of any new idle agent, MUST check its own background shell completions, and MUST re-run index:build / index:embed when a plan edit landed without a confirmed successful index rebuild.
followup_action: (a) For 00-helping / agent-maintenance-coordinator: a durable background-queue ledger in the session store (one row per dispatched agent with its expected slice, dispatch time and last observed status) would turn notification loss into a bounded reconciliation instead of an hours-long stall; the orchestrator reconciliation loop then reads only the ledger rows whose agent is not confirmed running. (b) For orchestrators at every tier: after waking from a session boundary, ALWAYS assume notifications may have been lost and start with one list_agents cross-check plus a background-shell completion check before dispatching anything new. (c) For planning: a slice that dispatches one background implementation agent per slice (the slim dispatch mandate) amplifies the cost of a single lost notification, because the whole slice queue is serialized behind the orchestrator turn loop - queue recovery should be a standard first-turn action, not an incident response.

description: THE RED CONTRACT SCHEMA DOES NOT REQUIRE A DISCRIMINATING, CURRENTLY-FAILING OBSERVABLE, SO A STEP PACKET CAN BE AUTHORED WITH VACUOUS (GREEN-ON-ARRIVAL) CONTRACTS. The two NEW [PLANNED] packets in plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md - Step 14S (the MOMENTUM law, slice P1-momentum-red) and Step 14T (the TURN-RATE laws, slice P1-turnrate-red) - author 8 RED contracts (RED-1..RED-4 per step), but a fresh independent verification found that 5 of the 8 are ALREADY SATISFIED by the current build and are therefore GREEN-ON-ARRIVAL: 14S RED-2, 14S RED-3, 14S RED-4, 14T RED-2 and 14T RED-4. Only 14S RED-1 (the momentum law does not exist), 14T RED-1 (the turn rate grows with the speed) and 14T RED-3 (the turn-rate-percent channel does not exist) fail against the current source. ROOT CAUSE: the 7 ratified Step 14Q RED contracts ALL open with an explicit NON-VACUITY GUARD (both lanes must really slide), so a relational assertion can never be satisfied by a flat or zero lane; NEITHER 14S nor 14T requires such a guard, so a RELATIONAL contract (STRICTLY DEEPER at a higher speed / STRICTLY LOWER at a higher speed) carrying only a BOUNDS or a PRESERVATION guard was authored that today's build already satisfies.
evidence: (1) THE FIVE VACUOUS CONTRACTS: the independent verification of the 8 RED contracts in the two [PLANNED] packets (Step 14S slice P1-momentum-red at plan lines 3574-3580; Step 14T slice P1-turnrate-red at plan lines 3732-3738) found ALREADY GREEN against the current source: 14S RED-2 (the committed slide is STRICTLY DEEPER at a high speed than at a low speed and EXACTLY 0 at a standstill - already true because the slide ramps at the SPEED-PROPORTIONAL entry rate), 14S RED-3 (the slide stays inside the depth budget and the severity inside the closed unit interval - a pure BOUNDS guard the current model already satisfies), 14S RED-4 (the live tick applies the momentum - a RELATIONAL comparison that already holds), 14T RED-2 (the steer axis value the drift model reads is UNCHANGED and the softened user turn rate still produces a committed slide - the PRESERVATION half is already true) and 14T RED-4 (the AI adoption is BEHAVIOR-PRESERVING - a pure PRESERVATION contract). Only 14S RED-1, 14T RED-1 and 14T RED-3 fail. (2) THE RATIFIED PRECEDENT THAT PREVENTS VACUITY - all 7 Step 14Q RED contracts open with an explicit NON-VACUITY GUARD in examples/neatRacing/physics/drift.model.test.ts, asserted FIRST: both lanes must really slide at :1567-1569 (contract [RED-14Q-1-LAW-SPEED-AXIS] at :1543); the low-speed lane must really slide, a zero slide would satisfy the ceiling vacuously, at :1592-1594 ([RED-14Q-2-SPEED-PROPORTIONAL-DEPTH] at :1576); both lanes must REACH the target slip, otherwise the comparison would be vacuous, at :1621-1623 ([RED-14Q-3A-ENTRY-RAMP-SPEED] at :1606); and the same guard shape at :1653, :1690, :1726, :1748, :986 and :1114. NEITHER 14S nor 14T contains an equivalent guard, and 14S RED-2 and 14T RED-1 are exactly the STRICTLY-RELATIONAL shape that the 14Q guard exists to protect. (3) THE CONTRIBUTING GATE GAP - a [PLANNED] packet is INVISIBLE to the structural sub-gates: scripts/agent-customization/gates/step-packet.gate.mjs:100-101 skips every YAML block whose status is not WIP (if (statusValue !== 'WIP') continue;), and scripts/agent-customization/gates/plan-slice-quality.gate.mjs:74-78 does the same, so the consolidated slice-advancement gate reports a TRIVIAL 4/4 structural pass for a [PLANNED] packet that has never been executed. (4) NO MACHINE GATE TESTS THAT A RED CONTRACT ACTUALLY FAILS: scripts/agent-customization/gates/red-test-confirmation.gate.mjs is a Tier-2 standalone-descriptor that returns pass TRUE unconditionally (mode: standalone-descriptor, minimumRedTests: 2) and never executes the contracts against the current source, so a vacuous RED contract cannot be caught by any gate in the inventory - only by an independent verification like this one.
followup_action: (a) SCHEMA (primary, for 01-planning): the RED contract schema must REQUIRE, in EVERY RED contract, (1) a DISCRIMINATING, CURRENTLY-FAILING observable - not only a bound, a preservation guard, or a relation that the current build already satisfies - and (2) a 14Q-style NON-VACUITY GUARD in every RELATIONAL lane (both lanes must really slide / both lanes must really turn), asserted FIRST so a flat or zero lane can never satisfy the comparison. (b) MACHINE CHECK (for agent-maintenance-coordinator): no gate in the current inventory verifies that a RED contract FAILS against the current source - a gate that re-runs the named RED suites of a packet and asserts that EVERY contract in the packet FAILS, reporting the per-contract failure names, would make vacuity DETECTABLE instead of reviewable-by-eye. (c) PACKET VISIBILITY (for agent-maintenance-coordinator): step-packet.gate.mjs and plan-slice-quality.gate.mjs skip non-WIP YAML blocks, so a [PLANNED] packet with a malformed or vacuous contract shape is structurally invisible; [PLANNED] packets should at least be checked for the required RED contract SHAPE (an id, a discriminating observable, and a non-vacuity guard wherever the contract is relational). (d) RE-OPEN TEMPLATE (bonus): carry the ratified 14Q RE-OPEN template (the ratified pin is DELETED and REPLACED in the SAME change) into the CONTRACT TEXT of every RED contract that re-opens a ratified surface, not only into the red_test rationale and the orchestrator_note, so the re-opening survives a copy-paste of the contract alone. (e) IMMEDIATE: the five vacuous contracts (14S RED-2, 14S RED-3, 14S RED-4, 14T RED-2, 14T RED-4) must be RE-AUTHORED or DROPPED before either packet is advanced to [WIP] - [PLANNED] is the last cheap moment.

description: The `plan` corpus family of the Cortex index is `plans/**/*.md` (ignoring `plans/completed/**`), NOT `plans/*.plans.md`, so the plan-family stale set can contain NON-`.plans.md` members: a targeted reindex that passes only `plans/<name>.plans.md` leaves `plans/README.md` and `plans/Roadmap.md` stale and the `cortex-index` gate STILL FAILS. The repair must target EVERY stale path the gate reports, not the one `.plans.md` file. Separately, `embed-index.mjs` configures NO busyTimeout on its libSQL client, so transient replica-lock contention surfaces as an immediate `SQLITE_BUSY: database is locked` exit 1 that must be retried externally and never resolved by killing the holder.

description: THE NEATRACING LANE PROGRAM LOADS NO GLOBAL-DECLARATION AMBIENT TYPE SOURCES, SO THE FIRST EXAMPLES->SRC IMPORT BREAKS THE ENTIRE LANE. When the P2-S3-A runtime adaptation engine pulled src network types (transitively via network.ts -> the GPU modules), tsconfig.neatRacing.json - which narrows include to examples/neatRacing/** and pins types: ["jest","node"] - left the sole declare-global block (src/architecture/network/gpu/gpu.types.d.ts:10: GPUDevice/GPUBuffer/...) out of the lane program, producing ~180 TS2304 errors across the lane. The eslint-legal fix is a binding-free emit-erased type-only module import (import type {} from ../../../src/architecture/network/gpu/gpu.types) carrying a 20-line rationale block comment; the triple-slash alternative (/// <reference path=...>) is banned by the recommended preset (@typescript-eslint/triple-slash-reference, path: never) while /// <reference lib=...> stays allowed. Reviewer wording nits recorded: the operative cause is the narrowed INCLUDE, not the types pinning per se, and "first examples->src import" holds at lane-program level only (sibling test files also import src).
evidence: examples/neatRacing/ai/runtime.adaptation.ts lines 1-21 (rationale comment + the type-only import); pre-fix lane failure ~180 TS2304 GPUDevice/GPUBuffer vs post-fix npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.neatRacing.json EXIT 0 + npx eslint examples/neatRacing/ai EXIT 0 (and the ambient anchor verified load-bearing: removing it reintroduces the TS2304 set); the FULL-severity specialist-review loop (R1 REQUEST_CHANGES comment-only fix -> R2 APPROVE) recorded in the P2-S3-A PlanUpdate in plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md (2026-11-06).
