description: THE NGE GROWTH PATH RANDOMIZES HIDDEN-NODE ACTIVATIONS FROM BARE Math.random() - A SRC-LEVEL DETERMINISM GAP WITH NO RNG HOOK, COMPENSATED AT THE ENGINE LAYER. NGE growth adds hidden nodes via network.mutate.handlers.utils.ts createHiddenNode (~:145-149), which calls node-level mutate(MOD_ACTIVATION) -> applyActivationMutation (src/architecture/node/node.ts:164) drawing the squash from bare Math.random() (verified: MUTATION_HANDLER_TABLE and the function body expose no rng hook, and the default method set has multiple entries so the draw is live), so every growth-added hidden node carried a RANDOM activation and post-growth scoring drifted across twin engines AND repeat runs even with a fully-seeded pipeline. Root-cause methodology that found it (reusable): probe-driven bisection with geneId-stripped JSON equality (Network twins differ only in cosmetic geneId fields from a shared global counter), repeated-run comparison, then node-level field comparison which showed biases/weights bit-identical while squashes randomized per run/instance (sinusoid/absolute/relu vs bipolar/sinusoid/softsign etc.). P2-S3-A engine-layer compensation (the activation-policy-immutability contract): capture pre-growth squashes beside the rollback bookkeeping, restore them post-cycle for surviving nodes, pin the Node default (Activation.logistic) for growth-added nodes BEFORE any post-mutation scoring - twin decision replay becomes bit-reproducible at zero RNG-stream cost. CAVEAT for later slices: Node.toJSON serializes squash.name while Node.fromJSON resolves squash by KEY (node.ts ~:1513 / ~:1544-1554), so a JSON round-trip restores activations as identity (pre-existing, silent).
evidence: the twin-decision-replay tests RED pre-fix -> GREEN post-fix (examples/neatRacing/ai/runtime.adaptation.test.ts ~:253 and ~:286; lane 69/69 final); probe methodology constraints recorded in the P2-S3-A PlanUpdate: jest probes must live inside testMatch trees (src/benchmarks/examples/testing - never tmp/), console output requires JEST_ALLOW_ALL_LOGS=1 via cmd /c (testing/jest-setup.ts suppression), probes deleted after use; the full finding chain is recorded in the P2-S3-A PlanUpdate in plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md (2026-11-06).
followup_action: (a) a src/architecture slice can own the rng hookup for applyActivationMutation (thread a mutation rng through MUTATION_HANDLER_TABLE) - an orchestrator-routed decision, src is outside the examples-only packet boundaries; (b) every NeatRacing growth-adjacent slice must keep the activation-policy-immutability canonicalization on its growth path; (c) Node.fromJSON squash-by-key vs toJSON squash.name is a pre-existing serialization asymmetry candidate for a later src bug-slice.

description: THE '**Required validation:**' PROSE MUST SPELL EVERY COMMAND OUT VERBATIM - A DEICTIC REFERENCE BACKTICKED THE WORD `validation`, SO THE PROSE-TO-YAML COMPARISON RETURNED A SINGLE PHANTOM TOKEN: the Step-23 and Step-23B packets' `**Required validation:**` prose read 'the four step `validation` lanes above', so mcp-plan-utils' extractRequiredValidationCommands (scripts/agent-customization/mcp/mcp-plan-utils.mjs:468-476 - it scans the prose section for BACKTICK SPANS with /`([^`]+)`/gu; it does not read natural language) returned ['validation'] instead of the five lane commands, and the workflow/validation MCP reported validationCommandsMatch: false. THE AUTHORISATION PATH WAS UNAFFECTED (run_allowlisted_validation authorises against the YAML `validation` list, never the prose), so the false mismatch was a DRIFT REPORT, never a gate blocker. THE FIX (the authoring rule): spell each lane command out VERBATIM in the prose, one backticked span per YAML `validation` entry, and NEVER backtick a non-command token such as the word `validation` (nor a count word like 'four'/'three') - a deictic 'the N lanes above' is invisible to the extractor.

description: THE EDIT TOOL'S PARAMETER LAYER IS A PARTIAL ESCAPE DECODER: IT DECODES THE \r AND \n ESCAPES IN old_str/new_str BUT DOES NOT UNESCAPE BACKSLASHES, AND ITS WRITE PATH NORMALIZES LINE ENDINGS TO CRLF. THREE CONSEQUENCES, ALL MEASURED IN THE STEP-23B B-4 PATCH CYCLE: (1) A BACKSLASH IS LITERAL - THE RAW-BACKSLASH COUNT IN old_str IS THE LITERAL-BACKSLASH COUNT THAT IS MATCHED: a 2-raw-backslash old_str matches a run of 2 literal backslashes, while 3, 4 and 8 raw backslashes match NOTHING; (2) AN OVERSIZED old_str DEGENERATES TO A SAFE NO-OP - it neither writes nor errors, the bytes simply never change (the failure is SILENT and a success message is returned); (3) THE REPAIR PATTERN IS THE CHUNKED-SENTINEL EDIT - cut the target region at unique sentinel boundaries and land ONE SMALL, BACKSLASH-LIGHT CHUNK PER EDIT instead of one giant old_str. THE LESSON FOR PLAN-TRACKER AUTHORING: SIZE AND ESCAPE EVERY EDIT DELIBERATELY - ANCHOR ON A SHORT, BACKSLASH-FREE, OCCURRENCE-VERIFIED UNIQUE LINE; NEVER TRUST THE EDIT TOOL'S SUCCESS MESSAGE; RE-READ THE TARGET RANGE AFTER EVERY EDIT.

description: RE-INDENTING A PlanUpdate YAML SECTION WITH THE edit TOOL BY ANCHORING ON THE INDENT IS UNSAFE: an indent-only anchor is a PARTIAL-LINE PREFIX anchor, so it can match the WRONG occurrence, it can silently NO-OP while the tool reports success, and it cannot express or match the artifacts it leaves behind (a bare CR 0x0D is untypeable in a literal old_str, and a shell-side rewrite is out of contract for an agent role). description: THE BATCH-175 TRACKER-ARCHIVAL PASS (EVIDENCE BATCH 175 IN plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.logs.md) TAUGHT A TRANSACTIONAL-ROLLBACK DEFECT CLASS THAT THE PRIOR MECHANISM EVENT DOES NOT COVER: A VERIFICATION STEP THAT CANNOT ROLL BACK IS NOT A TRANSACTION, IT IS A COIN FLIP. THE ARCHIVAL SCRIPT WROTE ITS BACKUPS, WROTE BOTH FILES, THEN VERIFIED - AND ITS ASSERT HELPER WAS IMPLEMENTED AS process.exit(1) INSIDE A try BLOCK; A process.exit INSIDE A try SKIPS THE catch, SO THE ROLLBACK NEVER RAN: WHEN A POST-WRITE ASSERTION FAILED, THE PLAN AND THE LOG WERE LEFT IN THE WRITTEN STATE, THE SCRIPT REPORTED FAILURE AND LEFT A HALF-TRANSFORMED PAIR ON DISK, AND THE ONLY RECOVERY PATH WAS THE tmp/ BACKUP BECAUSE git restore IS BANNED IN THIS REPO. THE FIX THAT MADE THE ROLLBACK REAL IS THAT THE ASSERTION HELPER MUST throw, SO THE catch CAN RESTORE BOTH FILES FROM THE PRE-WRITE BACKUP. THE SECOND-ORDER HAZARD FOLLOWS DIRECTLY: BECAUSE THE FAILED RUN LEFT THE FILES WRITTEN, THE NEXT RETRY OPERATED ON THE ALREADY-MODIFIED PLAN AND THE ANCHOR-UNIQUENESS GUARD FIRED SPURIOUSLY ('section prefix not unique: ## The ad-hoc audit') - A MISLEADING DIAGNOSTIC THAT POINTED AT THE ANCHORS WHEN THE REAL CAUSE WAS THE RESIDUE OF THE FAILED PRIOR RUN; AFTER ANY FAILED WRITE THE PRE-WRITE BACKUP MUST BE RESTORED BEFORE RETRYING, AND THE ANCHOR-UNIQUENESS ASSERTION MUST RUN AGAINST THE RESTORED FILE, BECAUSE A UNIQUENESS FAILURE CAN BE A RESIDUE SYMPTOM AND NOT AN ANCHOR DEFECT. THE THIRD DEFECT IS A LINE-ENDING ONE: THE PROSE/PLACEHOLDER FILE WAS CREATED WITH THE create TOOL, WHICH WRITES CRLF, AND THE SCRIPT BLOCK-MARKER REGEX WAS LINE-ANCHORED (/^<<<BLOCK: (.+)>>>$/), SO AGAINST A CRLF FILE IT MATCHED NOTHING AND THE RUN FAILED WITH 'prose block missing'; ANY LINE-ANCHORED PARSER OVER A TOOL-WRITTEN FILE MUST NORMALISE THE LINE ENDINGS FIRST (REPLACE EVERY CRLF PAIR WITH ONE LF), AND A 'CONTENT NOT FOUND' ERROR ON A FILE WHOSE CONTENT YOU CAN SEE IS A LINE-ENDING DEFECT BEFORE IT IS A CONTENT DEFECT. THIS IS THE SCRIPT/FILE VARIANT OF THE CRLF/CR FAMILY: learn-20261107-p2s3g1-edit-tool-bare-cr-untypeable-oldstr AND learn-20261107-p3s1b-edit-tool-multiline-lf-joined-oldstr-crlf-mismatch COVER THE EDIT-TOOL VARIANT, AND THE IDS THE DISPATCH PACKET NAMED FOR THAT FAMILY (BOTH learn-20261107-p3s3g1-...)
